episodes.196444: Multiple rounds of heavy rainfall and thunderstorms brought severe weather and flooding to southwest Missouri from November 4-5, 2024. A corridor of very heavy rainfall east of Springfield caused several rivers to reach major flood stage, with some locations experiencing record flooding. A total of four tornadoes were also observed on November 4, all of which were EF-0 in strength. Residual river flooding was observed through November 8, 2024 before flood waters began to recede.
episodes.196566: A cold front became a stationary front and stalled out across northern Arkansas leading to significant rainfall totals across northern Arkansas which led to numerous reports of flash flooding and significant rainfall totals.
episodes.196627: A plume of deep tropical moisture moved over the Hawaiian islands from east to west in association with a surface trough. This moisture combined with an upper level trough led to heavy rainfall, isolated thunderstorms, and flash flooding.
episodes.196653: A brief tornado occurred with a shower in Davis County during the late morning.  Weak instability along a modest boundary was sufficient for a small tornado from a shower producing EF0 damage.
episodes.196686: Wind convergence from a southeasterly breeze by a high pressure system centered to the south of American Samoa converged with northerly winds to the north of the territory. The instability from the wind convergence along with precipitable water above 2.5 inches brought flash flooding to the region along with numerous thunderstorms.
episodes.196734: Overnight on Sunday, November 3rd, a shield of rain and thunderstorms moved into the bi-state area. By Monday morning, persistent rainfall resulted in fatal flash flooding in southeast Missouri, with one fatality occurring in Iron County. Later on Monday evening, a QLCS produced two EF-0 tornadoes in east-central Missouri and shifted the axis of heaviest rain to the north. Due to the shift northward, record rainfall amounts caused deadly flash flooding in the St. Louis metropolitan area on Tuesday morning with two fatalities caused by rising waters.
episodes.197080: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed into and across northwestern Arkansas during the afternoon of the 4th, in an unseasonably moist and unstable air mass ahead of an approaching cold front. The atmosphere became very unstable ahead of the thunderstorms. The deep-layer and low-level wind shear strengthened during the afternoon, in response to a strong storm system translating into the Southern Plains from the Southern Rockies. The combination of very unstable air and very strong wind shear resulted in the development of some supercell thunderstorms, which produced several tornadoes across Benton and Washington Counties. Locally heavy rainfall resulted in flash flooding across portions of Benton, Madison, and Franklin Counties.
episodes.197230: Wet and unstable weather conditions persisted on Nov 5th onwards due to an upper-level trough and a surface frontal boundary through midweek, followed by the proximity of an area of low pressure by the 7th, heightening flooding and lightning risks. Flooding or Flash Flooding was reported in San Juan, Naguabo, Carolina and Guaynabo. A landslide was also reported on the 8th at Fajardo.
episodes.197403: A strong upper level trough generated multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms across North Texas on November 3 and 4. Most of the severe weather occurred on the 4th when the upper trough swept across the Plains and a cold front pushed through North and Central Texas. Damaging wind gusts was the primary severe weather occurrence, though large hail and flash flooding also occurred in a few instances.
episodes.197467: A cold front moved into a very warm, moist airmass and generated thunderstorms. Temperatures in the warm sector were near record highs when the front moved through. Some of the storms produced large hail and heavy rain that led to flash flooding.
episodes.197515: Thunderstorms developed ahead of an approaching cold front and short wave. Two tornadoes occurred.
episodes.197801: Multiple rounds of training heavy rain along a slow moving frontal boundary affected Southern and Eastern Missouri from the 4th through the 6th of November. Western fringes of the WFO Paducah county warning area in Carter County received 4-6 inches of rainfall in this span. Many locations further west and north from West Plains to Hillsboro in Missouri reached 7 to 10 inches of rainfall. Street flooding was reported in Van Buren early on the 5th. Water levels on the Current and St. Francis Rivers surged, reaching minor flood at Van Buren and Patterson while Doniphan went well into moderate flood, causing inundation of several structures on the 7th.
episodes.197968: Strong winds were reported along a line of showers just behind a cold front.
episodes.197981: Heavy rains led to river flooding on the White River in early November.
episodes.197984: Heavy rains led to river flooding on the Spring River in early November.
episodes.197985: Heavy rains led to river flooding on the Buffalo River in early November.
episodes.197986: Heavy rains led to river flooding on the Black River from early to mid November.
episodes.197988: A slow-moving frontal boundary brought several rounds of showers and thunderstorms to central Illinois from November 3rd through 5th.  Storm total rainfall during that time ranged from 2 to 4 inches, with a few locations across the Illinois River Valley picking up greater than 4 inches.  Due to antecedent drought conditions through September and October, much of the heavy rainfall readily soaked into the ground and caused little issue other than standing water in urban locations.  Localized flash flooding occurred under a viaduct in Champaign likely due to storm drains clogged with leaves and other debris.

events.narrative: Multiple Roads within Hilo and Mountainview were closed or partially closed due to flooding. Additionally, there was a vehicle submerged underwater on South Kopua Road in Punas Eden Roc neighborhood near Mountain View. The roads closed included Pohaku Dr, Enos Road, Mauna Loa Road, N Kulani Rd, Kahikopele St, Pohaku St between 39th Ave and 40th Av, Kamehameha Ave, Pauahi St, E Kawailani Rd.

A NWS storm survey confirmed that a brief EF-0 tornado with peak winds of 77 mph, a path length of 1.40 miles, and a width of 50 yards occurred 1 mile west-northwest of Elsey in Stone County. This tornado uplifted roofs to an outbuilding and outbuilding sheds, caused roof damage to both a church and a home, and snapped several large tree branches.

Route AB at Wolf Creek was closed due to flooding. Additional county property damages were reported throughout the entire county, primarily to dirt roads and bridges. Damage cost estimates are a reflection of the county as a whole.

Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding. Medina County 911 Dispatch received a call from an individual who was trapped in their vehicle that had been swept off Park Road 37 in high water at Mescal Creek. On the afternoon of the 5th, the vehicle was located about one mile downstream and the body of the driver 3-4 miles downstream just south of the Park Rd 37/FM 1283 intersection in Bandera County. The driver was a 20 year old male.
Portions of several roads were flooded near Withrow Springs State Park, and a swift water rescue was conducted to save stranded motorists.

A brief, weak tornado formed along Baptist Rd in Montgomery County, tracking east-northeastward. The tornado did not impact any structures, but produced sporadic tree damage and lofted crop debris that was sampled by the KLSX radar. The tornado was rated EF-0 and had a path length of 1.87 miles and a max path width of 25 yards. No deaths or injuries were reported.

A trained spotter provided pictures of water flooding many roads making them impassable along with water that had began to flood several local businesses. The nearby Harrison ASOS (KHRO) had recorded 5.39 inches of total rainfall for the calendar day.

An EF-0 tornado touched down just after 9:30pm CST on the evening of Monday, November 4th in northwestern St. Charles County. The tornado tracked to the northeast for just under 5 miles, damaging several trees, a pole barn and causing minor damage to a residence. It then tracked into southern Lincoln County. The tornado had a path length of 4.94 miles and a max path width of 75 yards in St. Charles County. No deaths or injuries were reported.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding closing Haby Ln. and Bandera Rd. along San Geronimo Creek.
Thunderstorms produced an estimated two to five inches of rain in three hours. This rain caused flash flooding closing Little Blanco Rd. near Twin Sisters.

The tornado then crossed Highway 61 from St. Charles County into far southern Lincoln County doing minor and isolated tree damage before lifting. The tornado had a path length of 1.14 miles and a max path width of 25 yards in Lincoln County. No deaths or injuries were reported.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding. There was a high water rescue of a vehicle stranded on Blanco Rd. at Meusebach Creek near Camp Bullis.
Route J was closed due to flash flooding from heavy rainfall.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding closing roads in northwestern San Antonio.
Thunderstorms produced heavy rain. San Antonio Fire Department rescued a person from a flooded drainage ditch near Tioga Dr. and I-10 in northwestern San Antonio.
Highway 76 was reported under water due to flash flooding from heavy rainfall.

Flash flooding resulted in cropland, yard, basement, and road flooding around Jefferson County. Water flooded residences in a mobile home park in High Ridge, with several homes and mobile homes being evacuated. Multiple water rescues were also reported in House Springs.
Minor flooding occurred along the St Francis river at Patterson. The flooding was mainly of bottomland and surrounding low-lying areas.

Heavy rain caused numerous road closures with vehicles stranded in St. Louis County. Multiple water rescues were reported from cars driving through flooded roadways. At Bayless and I-55, flash flooding from heavy rain and overflow from Gravois Creek resulted in two fatalities.

Numerous area creeks saw rapid rises due to persistent heavy rain. Overflowing creeks resulted in flooding of basements, yards, and cropland and also contributed to the 2 fatalities mentioned previously in this episode. Gravois Creek at Mehlville saw its highest crest ever recorded, with Deer Creek at Ladue and Grand Glaize Creek at Valley Park seeing their second highest crests on record.
Route N in Ozark County was closed due to flash flooding.
At least 6 inches of water covered the Fagaima Road between the TMO Hardware region and the Georgina Building. Water was seen flowing onto properties and flooding areas along the roadway.
Numerous low water crossings were flooded and impassible in northwestern Texas County.
Highway 23 was flooded and closed near the Mulberry River.
The Spring River at Imboden entered minor flood stage in early November with the crest of 20.87 feet occurring on November 5 at 6:00 PM CST.
Heavy rain caused water over major roadways such as I-44 at Nebraska Ave and I-70 at Carrie Avenue. On Skinker Blvd, vehicles were stranded due to flash flooding.

A bridge was washed out by flood water on Chickadee Lane in the Mountain Grove community. Flooding resulted in at least four residences landlocked in the Watalula area. Portions of Highway 23 were flooded and closed north of the Mulberry River Bridge near Turners Bend.

Highway Y at Cowskin Creek was closed due to flooding. Additional county property damages were reported throughout the entire county, primarily to dirt roads and bridges. Damage cost estimates are a reflection of the county as a whole.
Heavy rain caused water over Highways 19 and 8 on the east side of Steelville. A trooper also reported that the Meramec River was 4 feet over the road at Campbell Bridge on Highway N.

A vehicle driving on Highway H two miles east of Manes in Wright County was swept off the road into flood waters at Beaver Creek. The two occupants, ages 70 and 73 attempted to swim to dry ground and reportedly drowned.

A tornado touched down south of Log Cabin Road where it moved northeast and damaged a few trees. A bumper pull camper rolled over and an awning was ripped off of a house. The tornado crossed Highway 190 and directly hit a meat market where 3 people were injured. A cinder block wall fell over as roughly 25 percent of the roofing material was pulled off the building. An old barn was also damaged behind the meat market. The tornado was weakening as it crossed Stagg Avenue where there was minor tree damage along with damage to a couple of power poles. Maximum estimated winds were 95 mph.

events.narrative: Strong winds were reported along a line of showers behind a cold front.

The tornado touched down just west of Ben Road. It moved northeast where it destroyed a garage, a mobile home shifted off its foundation, and part of a roof was removed from a home. An old frame home was completely destroyed. The tornado continued to move northeast and crossed Fats Rd leaving debris across the roadway. The tornado then moved into Acadia Parish as it crossed Bayou Queue de Tortue. Maximum estimated winds were 105 mph.

The tornado continued north from Vermilion Parish across Bayou Queue de Tortue into Acadia Parish. The tornado  formed convergent patterns over a sugarcane field. It continued northeast and dissipated between Toups Road and Highway 35. The maximum estimated wind speed was 105 mph.

A brief tornado occurred south of Floris from a developing weak storm. The tornado moved across a farmstead on the west side of Pecan Avenue producing high end EF0 damage to two metal buildings. The tornado lifted shortly afterwards.
The Black River at Black Rock entered minor flood stage in early November and remained in minor flood stage into mid November with a crest of 21.41 feet which occurred on November 6 at 9:15 PM CST.
The Buffalo River at St. Joe entered minor flood stage in early November and ended up cresting in moderate flood stage of 35.44 feet on November 5 at 8:30 PM CST.

Additional damage occurred to roads and bridges across northern Pulaski County along the Roubidoux and Gasconade Rivers.
